I.A. No. 1 of 2022

And 
I.A. No. 1 of 2022
In
CRLA No. 432 of 2021
Shri Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, J.
Shri Alok Kumar Verma, J. 
Shri R.P. Nautiyal, learned Sr. Advocate 
assisted by Shri Pankaj Tangwan learned counsel 
for the appellant in Criminal Appeal No. 287 of 
2021 and Shri A.S. Rawat, learned Sr. Advocate 
assisted by Shri Naman Kamboj, learned counsel
the appellant in Criminal Appeal No. 432 of 
2021.
Shri J. S. Virk, learned Deputy Advocate 
General with Shri Rakesh Kumar Joshi, learned 
Brief Holder for the State.
These two applications have been filed by 
the appellants / applicants for suspension of 
sentence and grant of bail. The appellants have 
convicted under Sections 201, 302/120B of the 
Indian Penal Code, 1860 and sentenced them to 
undergo imprisonment for life and to pay fine of 
Rs. 25,000/- each and in default, to further 
undergo simple imprisonment of four months 
under Section 302 IPC; to undergo rigorous 
imprisonment for five years and to pay fine of 
Rs. 10,000 each and in default, to further undergo 
simple imprisonment of three months under 
Section 201 IPC.
Admittedly, the case of the prosecution is 
based on circumstantial evidence. It is apparent 
from the record that there is a last seen evidence 
against appellant – Snehlata Chauhan and she 
had made an extra judicial confession to PW5 
Smt. Rajkumari Chauhan, who is her sister in law (Jethani) and then there is recovery of purse 
of the deceased on the statement of appellant –
Amit Parley. Death of the deceased was 
determined to be homicidal in nature. Moreover, 
it is apparent from record that both the 
appellants were not on bail during trial.
Keeping in view the aforesaid 
circumstances, we are of the opinion that the 
arguments advanced by the respective learned 
Senior Counsel for the appellants are, in fact, 
matter to be considered regarding re￾appreciation of the evidence, at the final stage of
hearing of the appeals. At this stage, we are of 
the prima facie view that the judgment passed by 
the learned IV Additional Sessions Judge, 
Dehradun is correct and there is no need to 
suspend the sentence and grant bail to the 
appellants. 
In that view of the matter, we are inclined 
to dismiss the applications. Accordingly, both 
the applications are dismissed being devoid of 
merits. 
List these matters on 06.09.2022 for final 
disposal. 
In the meantime, learned counsel for the 
appellants shall obtain paper book from the 
Registry. 
 (Alok Kumar Verma, J.) (Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, J.)
 05.07.2022
SKS

in

Shri S.K.Mishra, ACJ.
Shri Alok Kumar Verma, J. 
 Mr. Naman Kamboj, learned counsel 
for the applicant.
Mr. J.S.Virk, learned Deputy A.G. for 
the State. 
This is a short term bail application 
filed by the appellant Amit Parley on the 
ground of medical illness. He has been 
convicted under Sections 302, 201 and 
120B IPC and sentenced for a term of life 
imprisonment.
On the last date, learned Deputy 
Advocate General was directed to take 
instructions. 
He has taken instructions and 
submits before the Court that the 
appellant was sustained a AC Joint Injury 
and he is recommended for treatment to 
surgical intervention. Copy of instructions 
is produced before us. 
The report of the Medical Officer, 
District Jail, Dehradun reveals that the 
patient is suffering from TINEA CRURES 
and Alopecia Aereata and that he is being 
treated regularly. 
In that view of the matter, we are 
inclined to grant short term bail of 45
days to the appellant-applicant. 
Let the applicant Amit Parley be 
released on short term bail for a period of 
45 days, which shall be reckoned from 
the date of his release from the jail, on 
such suitable terms and conditions, as  the learned 4th Additional Sessions Judge, 
Dehradun deems fit and proper, in 
Sessions Trial No. 144 of 2018, (State vs. 
Sneh Lata Chauhan & another), decided 
on 31.08.2018 and 02.09.2019. 
On expiry of 45 days, the appellant 
shall surrender before the Court, in turn, 
shall send him to jail. In case, he fails to 
surrender after expiry of 45 days, the 
learned 4th Additional Sessions Judge, 
Dehradun, shall issue non bailable 
warrant against the appellant. 
Urgent copy of this order be supplied 
to the learned counsel for the parties, as 
per Rules. 
(Alok Kumar Verma, J.) (S.K.Mishra, J.)
 07.09.2022 Kaushal

Hon’ble S.K. Mishra, J.
Hon’ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
Mr. R.P. Nautiyal, learned Senior 
Advocate assisted by Ms. Garima Thapa, 
learned counsel for the applicant/appellant.
Mr. J.S. Virk, learned Deputy Advocate 
General for the State.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
This Short Term Bail Application has been 
filed by the appellant- Snehlata Chauhan 
under Section 389 of the Code of Criminal 
Procedure, 1973. She has been convicted for 
the offence under Sections 302 read with 
Section 120B and 201 of the Indian Penal 
Code (hereinafter referred to as the “Penal 
Code”) by the learned IVth Additional Sessions 
Judge, Dehradun in Sessions Trial No. 144 of 
2018 by judgment dated 31.08.2021/
02.09.2021. Under Section 302 read with 
Section 120B of the Penal Code, she has been 
sentenced to undergo life imprisonment and 
also to pay a fine of Rs. 25,000/- and in 
default of payment of fine, to further undergo 
four months additional simple imprisonment 
and under Section 201 of the Penal Code, she 
has been sentenced to undergo life 
imprisonment for a period of five years and 
also to pay a fine of Rs. 10,000/- and in 
default of payment of fine, to further undergo 
three months additional simple imprisonment. 
All the sentences are directed to run 
concurrently. 
This short term bail application has been  filed by the appellant, who has undergone for 
life imprisonment for committing murder of 
her own husband on the ground that she has 
to make arrangements for the death-cum￾retirement benefit of his late husband in 
favour of her minor sons. She is also required
to file her income tax return and seeks income 
tax refund. 
Keeping in view the interest of the minor 
children of the appellant, the short term bail 
application is allowed. 
In that view of the matter, we are 
inclined to grant short term bail to the 
appellant for a period of 30 days. 
Let appellant, Snehalata Chauhan be 
released on short term bail for a period of 30 
days to be reckoned from the date of his 
release, on such terms and conditions as 
deemed just and proper by the learned IVth 
Additional Sessions Judge, Dehradun. On 
completion of 30 days, to be reckoned from
the date of release, she shall surrender before 
the learned trial court. On such an event she 
will be remanded to the custody. If she does 
not surrender, proper warrant shall be issued 
against him.
List this matter on 28.02.2023 for final 
disposal. 
(Alok Kumar Verma, J.) (Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, J.)
21.09.2022
Neha/SB

In
CRLA No.287 of 2021
Hon’ble S.K. Mishra, J.
Hon’ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
Mr. R.P. Nautiyal, learned Senior Advocate 
assisted by Ms. Garima Thapa, learned counsel 
for the applicant/appellant.
Mr. J.S. Virk, learned Deputy Advocate 
General for the State.
This is an application for extension of short 
term bail, granted by us on 21.09.2022, on the 
ground that the purpose for which he has been 
granted short term bail could not be completed. 
It is borne out from the record that the 
appellant-Snehlata Chauhan was granted short 
term bail by us so that she could secure legal 
heirs certificate for her children and also get the 
GPF and other death-cum-retirement benefits of 
her late husband in her favour and also to get 
Income Tax refund. It is submitted that though 
she succeeded in getting the Income Tax refund 
but the other two duties i.e. the legal heirs 
certificate and release of death-cum-retirement 
benefits could not be worked out. Hence, she is 
prayed for an extension of short term bail. 
We are inclined to grant extension of 
short term bail to the appellant for a period of
30 days on the same bail bond executed by him
on 21.09.2022. 
It is stated that the short term bail granted 
by us earlier comes to its logical conclusion 
today. Hence, the appellant is granted 
extension till 15th December, 2022. 
On 16.12.2022, she shall surrender before 
the learned trial court. On such an event, she  will be remanded to the custody. If she does 
not surrender, proper warrant shall be issued 
against her.
The matter be listed on 28.02.2023 as 
fixed by us earlier. 
Let a certified copy of this order be issued 
to the learned counsel for the parties, today 
itself, on payment of usual charges. 
(Alok Kumar Verma, J.) (Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, J.)
15.11.2022
Neha/SB

Snehlata Chauhan --Appellant
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand --Respondent
With
CRLA No.432 of 2021
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Hon’ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Mr. Amar Murti Shukla, learned counsel for the 
appellant in CRLA No.287 of 2021 and Mr. M. K. Ray, 
learned Amicus Curiae for the appellant in CRLA No.432 of 
2021. 
2. Mr. Siddhartha Bisht, learned A.G.A for the State. 
3. Instant appeal is preferred against the judgment and 
order dated 31.08.2021/02.09.2021, passed in Sessions Trial 
No.144 of 2018, State vs. Snehlata Chauhan & Anr., by the 
court of learned 4th Additional Sessions Judge, Dehradun. By 
it, the appellant has been convicted under Sections 302, 201 
and 120-B of IPC. 
4. The appellant, Snehlata Chauhan seeks short term bail 
on the ground that her two children are suffering from 
depression and the younger one has to be admitted in Class 
10th as he did not write his examination last year.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that 
appellant's two children, Sarthak Chauhan and Shaurya 
Pratap Singh Chauhan, are staying with their grandmother 
and grandfather; they are suffering from depression. The 
Child Welfare Committee, District Dehradun on 12.06.2026 
had given a report to that effect. The children are passing 
through psychological trauma due to the loss of their father 
and mother being in jail. Therefore, it is argued that the 
appellant may be released on short-term bail for some time  so that she could get her younger son admitted in Class 10th
and give them some company so that they could be 
emotionally a little strong to wade through their life.
6. Learned State counsel is required to get a report. 
Learned State Counsel submits that in fact the children of the 
appellant, Snehlata Chauhan, are staying with her parents.
There is no material on record to controvert the report of 
Child Welfare Committee, which is Annexure-2 to the short￾term bail application.
7. We have carefully gone through the CWC report, 
which records that the children of the appellant are suffering 
from depression and they are also going through emotional 
trauma. The report also records that if timely guidance is not 
given, the possibility of their coming into contact with anti￾social elements may not be ruled out.
8. Having considered, purely on humanitarian ground, 
the short term bail is granted to the appellant Snehlata 
Chauhan for a period of three weeks from the date of her
release, subject to her executing a personal bond and 
furnishing two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to 
the satisfaction of the court concerned. 
9. It is further directed that on expiry of the duration of 
short term bail, the appellant shall surrender before the court 
concerned.
10. List these matters on 04.11.2026
11. Let a copy of this order be immediately forwarded to 
the court and jail concerned through e-mail with a request 
that after obtaining e-true copy of it, necessary action may be 
initiated so that the release of the appellant is not delayed. 
(Siddhartha Sah, J.) (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
